Subject: Dedicated capacity request — long-context LLM POC

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks for taking this on. Quick background: Zephyr is running a retrieval-augmented generation flow where the active context window can reach 80k–120k tokens (compressed shards + retrieved docs). We want a POC on dedicated pods to serve a steady-state 25 TPS with 95th percentile bursts to 50 TPS during business hours. Expected generation per request: initial prompt ~5–20k tokens, then model generates up to 1k tokens.

Key asks:
- Sizing guidance (GPU count and headroom) for an 8–16B and a 65B model family we plan to evaluate.
- Tradeoffs if we apply 4-bit (q4) weight quantization and separate strategies for KV cache (keep in FP16/FP32 vs quantized KV).
- Any pinned pod configs we should request for predictable latency and for compliance (VPC).

Attached: zephyr_capacity_request.pdf (workload profile) and kv_memory_trace.csv (sample token-by-token key/value growth from a week of traffic).

We can do a call tomorrow if helpful — Rajiv (cc) will loop in procurement when we have a ballpark cost.

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — long-context LLM POC

Amy — thanks for the details and the attachments, the traces are especially helpful. High-level takeaways and an initial sizing sketch below.

Quick assumptions we used for the sketch:
- Two model families under consideration: Zephyr-8B (decoder-only 8B) and Zephyr-65B (decoder-only 65B).
- Target sustained 25 TPS (burst to 50 TPS). Average generation length ~500 tokens per request; KV carry-through equals prompt tokens (so KV grows with the 5–20k prompt window).
- Using NVIDIA A100 80GB class GPUs in reserved pods unless otherwise requested.

Initial sizing (ordered by questions):
1) Memory profile (per-GPU, ballpark):
   - Zephyr-8B (FP16 weights + FP16 KV): model weights + optimizer state ~ 16–24 GB; KV cache for 100k tokens ~ 40–48 GB (depends on hidden size). Total resident memory ~60–72 GB. With modest headroom (25%), we recommend 1 model replica per GPU and 1–2 GPUs per serving slot for concurrency, so a 3–4 GPU reserved pool for steady 25 TPS with headroom.
   - Zephyr-65B (FP16 weights + FP16 KV): model weights ~ 70–85 GB; KV cache for 100k tokens ~ 40–80 GB (depends on KV packing). Total ~130–165 GB — exceeds a single 80GB GPU so we assume model sharding + KV offload. Practical reserved configuration: 4–6 x A100-80GB per serving replica to hit steady 25 TPS with planned batching. For 50 TPS burst capacity, plan a reserved pool sized for sustained 25 TPS plus autoscale buffer or a hot-standby of 1–2 extra replicas (equivalent to another 4–6 GPUs).

2) Quantization / KV strategies and impact:
   - q4 (4-bit) weight quantization reduces weight table to ~40–50% of FP16 weight memory (very model-dependent). For Zephyr-65B weight memory can drop to ~35–45 GB, which can reduce the number of GPUs required for model-sharded deployments by ~1.5–2x.
   - KV cache is more sensitive: quantizing KV (e.g., to 8-bit or 4-bit) saves memory but risks numeric degradation in long-chain attention and retrieval alignment. We recommend a hybrid approach for POC: q4 for weights + 8-bit (or bf16 packed) for KV cache. That typically yields ~30–40% total resident memory reduction while keeping quality regressions small in our tests.

3) Headroom & operational recommendations: 
   - Safety headroom: 25–35% reserved on top of steady-state for traffic spikes and model rollouts.
   - Canary & fallback: start with q4 weights + FP16 KV in canary, compare generation similarity metrics (per your eval set), then flip to quantized KV if quality delta < threshold (we usually use 0.5% ROUGE/embedding-similarity delta).
   - Autoscale policy: keep core reserved capacity for 25 TPS and allow burst to shared pool; set hard-limit routing to fall back to a smaller-model variant if headroom exhausted.

4) Latency and cost notes:
   - Long-context workloads are dominated by KV read/write and attention indexing rather than pure forward FLOPs. Expect cold-start latencies higher when KV must be recovered; warm steady-state per-token latency is modest. Exact p95 depends on batching and attention optimizations.
   - Cost: moving Zephyr-65B from FP16->q4 often reduces monthly reserved GPU cost by 30–50% due to fewer GPUs and higher packing efficiency. We'll provide a numeric cost comparison when you confirm model family and desired quality thresholds.

Next steps we propose:
- Internal sizing spreadsheet (attached) with per-model, per-config GPU counts and cost estimates (I attached initial_sizing.xlsx).
- Short technical workshop tomorrow to align on quality threshold for KV quantization (30–45 minutes).
- If procurement wants rough contract language for reserved pods + burst terms, Laura can draft.

Cc'ing Laura and Dev to help with contract and throughput tests. Happy to jump on a call — what time works for you tomorrow?

Thanks,

Amy / Rajiv — following our workshop and the quick internal run, here are concrete follow-ups and the 90-day / 12-month estimates you asked for. I include the canary plan and the quality metric example.

A) Clarifications on architecture:
- The 4–6 GPUs per replica estimate for Zephyr-65B assumes model sharding across GPUs with KV stored primarily in GPU memory for fastest steady-state latency. If you keep KV in host memory and stream, expect higher tail latency and additional CPU/network I/O — that can reduce per-replica GPU count but will increase latency and complexity. For the POC we recommend GPU-resident KV for the first canary run, then evaluate host-memory KV if memory limits force it.

B) Canary / quality measurement (example):
- Dataset: your 150 human-judged prompts + extra 250 synthetic edge prompts we supply.
- Metrics: embedding-similarity (mean cosine) between baseline FP16-KV output and candidate quantized configuration; human-preference delta on a 3-judge blind subset.
- Thresholds we suggest: mean embedding cosine >= 0.995 and <5% human-preference loss on critical flows. If thresholds fail, keep FP16-KV and iterate on 8-bit KV compression.

C) Ballpark cost (USD) — all numbers assume A100-80GB reserved pricing and include a 30% operational/headroom uplift:
- Zephyr-8B (baseline reserved for 25 TPS): 4 x A100-80GB reserved pool ~ $16k/month (90-day ~ $48k). With 50% burst buffer (+2 GPUs) ~ $24k/month. 12-month committed discount estimates available on request.
- Zephyr-65B (FP16, GPU-resident KV): baseline reserved (25 TPS) ~ 20 x A100-80GB ~ $80k/month. With 50% burst headroom and a hot-standby replica, plan ~ 30 x A100-80GB ~ $120k/month.
- Zephyr-65B (q4 weights + 8-bit KV hybrid): baseline reserved ~ 12–16 x A100-80GB ~ $48k–$64k/month (90-day proportional estimate $144k–$192k). This is our estimate for moving from FP16 to q4 weight quantization and modest KV compression.

D) Recommended next steps & timeline:
1) Sign SOW addendum for a 6-week POC (testbed + canary) — Redwood provides instrumentation and 2-week quality evaluation.
2) Week 1–2: deploy q4-weights + FP16-KV canary, run evals.
3) Week 3: if metrics pass, enable 8-bit KV and re-evaluate on the same eval set.
4) Week 4–6: capacity soak tests and finalize reserved capacity counts.

I will ask Marissa to draft a short SOW and Laura to pull in procurement language for reserved + burst. If you want, we can include an optional clause for a quarterly capacity re-eval so you can move between quantization profiles without renegotiating core terms.

Thanks — see attached updated sizing sheet (I updated the per-config GPU rows).
